title: QL-1.04 The claims check runs in every repository from one script: a claim ahead of its status row fails CI
request: Closes quality-loop principle 4 (CI fails in any repo, site included, if a claim runs ahead of its row). Repository: memev. Depends on contracts: SR-5.04. Quality-loop principle set of 30 October 2026 (owner's order: implement as a gate for all dev). Sequenced with QL-1.03, which also changes .github/workflows/ci.yml. The fixtures follow SR-5.04's status table as merged.

tasks.title: One claims checker
requirements: scripts/gate/claims.mjs reads the status table of SR-5.04 (docs/status.json, or the path given by --status) and scans the files given by --surfaces (globs) for each feature's claim phrases; a feature whose row is planned and appears without the planned label, or a performance figure without a results file named in its row, is a finding
a planned row without a date older than four weeks is a warning and older than eight weeks is a finding that says give it a date, drop it, or move it to the roadmap (principle 5)
--json prints {features, claims, findings, warnings}; exit 1 on any finding; no dependencies; a version: comment on the first line

claims.mjs exits 2, distinct from 1 for a finding, and prints the cause when the status file is missing, is not valid JSON, has no feature rows, holds a status outside the documented set, or has no claim phrases, and when a --surfaces glob matches no file; --json reports the number of files scanned under the key files

claims.mjs and every file it imports only read files: they spawn no process, open no network connection, resolve no name, write nothing, and import only node:fs, node:path, node:url, node:process and ./ files under scripts/gate/ that obey the same rule; none uses createRequire, require(, process.binding, process.dlopen, WebSocket, EventSource, globalThis[ or import(

a planned feature counts as labelled only when the label sits in the same sentence or HTML element as its claim phrase; each Markdown list item, table row and HTML li, tr and td is its own unit whatever its punctuation, and a label in one does not cover another; the one exception is an element of class tag whose whole text is the label, which labels the next sibling element only (the site's section tag); 'not planned', 'was planned', 'as planned' and 'no longer planned' are not the label; phrases match without regard to case, across line wraps, with HTML tags stripped, entities decoded, Markdown emphasis and link syntax removed (the link text kept), Unicode hyphens folded to '-' and typographic apostrophes and quotes folded to ASCII

a performance figure is a number, with thousands separators or a k suffix allowed, followed by a unit of time, throughput or size (ms, s, seconds, MB, GB, ops/s, req/s, x or × faster) in a sentence; it needs a results file that exists, named in the row of the feature the sentence names, and a figure sentence that names no feature is a finding; version numbers, durations such as a 14-day trial, prices and counts are not figures; a sentence carrying the marker <!-- claims: not a figure --> is exempt from this rule only
the age of a planned row comes from a field in the row (the date it was marked planned), never from a file time or git history; claims.mjs takes --now so tests fix the clock
the fixtures follow SR-5.04's status table as merged, and the CLI is tested end to end on fixtures at fixed paths

a planned row whose 'marked planned' field is missing, not an ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) or after --now makes claims.mjs exit 2 naming the row; a planned row whose target date is before --now is a finding naming the row, whatever its age

a --surfaces file of any other type (.mdx, .astro, .txt and so on) is scanned as plain text with HTML tags stripped, never skipped; with no --surfaces, claims.mjs scans README.md, **/*.md and **/*.html under the working directory, leaving out node_modules/ and .git/, and --json says which globs it used
when one row's phrase lies inside another row's phrase at the same place, only the longer phrase counts there

each red-green criterion of this task that runs test/gate-claims.test.mjs has its own subtest whose name starts with <task>-cNN: (NN is the criterion's position in this task, so T1-c01: for the first), and the criterion runs only that subtest

criteria.statement: A fixture page claiming a planned feature without its label fails; the same page with the label passes; a planned row nine weeks old without a date fails and five weeks old warns

tasks.title: Shipped to the other repositories
requirements: scripts/gate/sync-gates.mjs copies scripts/gate/** into a target checkout given by --to and prints the version of each file copied; a target whose copy is older than this repository's is reported
docs/DEVELOPING.md says the gate scripts are owned here and copied into memev-site, memev-cloud, memev-org and memev-ops, and that each of them runs claims.mjs in its CI
sync-gates.mjs copies docs/status.json with the gate scripts, and claims.mjs reads the status table only from the copy in its own checkout

sync-gates.mjs --check writes nothing and exits non-zero naming the file when a target gate file differs in content from this repository's (even at the same version line), is missing, or has no version line; versions compare numerically (1.10 is newer than 1.9), and a newer target copy is reported, never overwritten; docs/status.json, which cannot carry a version line, is exempt from the version-line rule only and is compared by content like every gate file, and so is each results file sync copies

memev's own CI runs claims.mjs over README.md, docs/**/*.md and site/**/*.html, the globs quoted so claims.mjs expands them itself, on every pull request that touches them and on a schedule, so the age rule runs even when nothing changes: the claims step sits in a job whose if: admits both schedule and pull_request, after no step that reads github.base_ref, passes no --now, and the scheduled run has a concurrency group of its own

sync-gates.mjs --check also exits non-zero, naming the repository, when no workflow under the target's .github/workflows/ runs node scripts/gate/claims.mjs; memev's CI has a scheduled job that checks out memev-site, memev-cloud, memev-org and memev-ops read-only, with a read-only token held as a repository secret (an owner step), and runs sync-gates.mjs --to <checkout> --check on each; the job fails, never skips, when the secret is missing
sync-gates copies every results file named in a row of docs/status.json to the same path in the target, so a figure backed in memev is backed in the target

each sentence of README.md, docs/**/*.md and site/**/*.html that gives hardware or limits rather than performance (for example docs/testing/LAB-TEST-PLAN.md's '2 CPUs, 4 GB RAM, 10 GB disk') carries the marker <!-- claims: not a figure --> at the end of its line; apart from docs/DEVELOPING.md, T2 changes those files only by inserting the marker

each red-green criterion of this task that runs test/gate-sync.test.mjs has its own subtest whose name starts with <task>-cNN: (NN is the criterion's position in this task, so T2-c01: for the first), and the criterion runs only that subtest

criteria.statement: sync-gates.mjs --to <dir> --check writes nothing (the target's file hashes are unchanged afterwards) and exits non-zero, naming the file, when: a target gate file has the same version line but different sha256 content; a gate file is missing in the target; or the target copy has no version line. It exits 0 only when every file is byte-identical to this repository's. Residual risk that no criterion here can cover: a PR that edits its own copy is caught only if this check runs from outside that PR (a scheduled memev job over the four repositories, or CODEOWNERS on scripts/gate/** in each target).

criteria.statement: Run claims.mjs in the CI's form (README.md, 'docs/**/*.md', 'site/**/*.html'), capture its own exit code (must be 0), and require features > 0, claims > 0, zero findings, and the files-scanned count (key 'files'; the requirement should name the key) equal to the number of files find lists for README.md, docs/**/*.md and site/**/*.html.

verifier.cmd: want=$({ ls README.md; find docs -type f -name '*.md'; find site -type f -name '*.html'; } | wc -l); out=$(node scripts/gate/claims.mjs --json --surfaces README.md 'docs/**/*.md' 'site/**/*.html'); rc=$?; [ "$rc" = 0 ] || exit 1; printf '%s' "$out" | W=$want node -e "const r=JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync(0,'utf8'));const n=x=>Array.isArray(x)?x.length:Number(x);process.exit(n(r.features)>0&&n(r.claims)>0&&n(r.findings)===0&&n(r.files)===Number(process.env.W)?0:1)"

criteria.statement: Apart from docs/DEVELOPING.md, every file under README.md, docs/ and site/ that differs from the recorded base, untracked files included, is an existing file whose head copy, with each ' <!-- claims: not a figure -->' (and the spaces before it) removed, equals its base copy byte for byte.

verifier.cmd: [ -n "$MEMEV_CONTRACT_BASE" ] && b=$(mktemp) && h=$(mktemp) && ok=1 && for f in $({ git diff --name-only "$MEMEV_CONTRACT_BASE" -- README.md docs site; git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -- README.md docs site; } | sort -u | grep -vxF docs/DEVELOPING.md); do git cat-file -e "$MEMEV_CONTRACT_BASE:$f" 2>/dev/null || { echo "new file: $f"; ok=0; continue; }; git show "$MEMEV_CONTRACT_BASE:$f" > "$b"; [ -f "$f" ] || { echo "deleted: $f"; ok=0; continue; }; sed "s/ *<!-- claims: not a figure -->//g" "$f" > "$h"; cmp -s "$b" "$h" || { echo "changed beyond markers: $f"; ok=0; }; done; [ "$ok" = 1 ]
